notes.title: CryptPad: when the key ships with the ciphertext
notes.summary: A Windows 'encrypted notepad' sandwiches RC4 between two XOR passes, then appends the random key to every file it writes.

notes.title: FLRSCRNSVR: peeling a screensaver's three-stage cipher
notes.summary: A 64-bit .scr hides a 25-character check behind junk code. Undoing a reversal, a position-dependent XOR and a substitution recovers the flag.

notes.title: RecordPlayer: fixing two hidden switches with a two-byte patch
notes.summary: The audio plays as noise because direction and pitch are hard-coded to the wrong values. Two bytes in x64dbg make it play the flag.

notes.title: httpd: an ICMP-triggered backdoor behind an HTTP decoy
notes.summary: A Go binary for FreeBSD waits for a magic ping and builds its AES key from packet fields. Most of those fields turn out to be predictable.

notes.title: connected: talking to a simulated network of oracles
notes.summary: A small C++ network simulator. The orchestrator wants a message whose checksum lands on one constant, so I brute-forced an 8-byte palindrome.

notes.title: What Did You Type: from USB keystrokes to decrypted exfiltration
notes.summary: Keystrokes in a USB capture lead to a dropper, a reflective loader and a file-stealing agent whose AES keys travel alongside the stolen files.

notes.title: wallpaper: meet-in-the-middle on a 1 KB state machine
notes.summary: A syscall-only ELF checks a 37-digit base-4 password through an invertible state machine. A forward BFS and a backward DFS meet in the middle.

notes.title: moment.exe: a static solve past 17 anti-analysis checks
notes.summary: Heavy anti-debugging, encoded strings and an event-gated flag path. Rebuilding the string table and reading call-site arguments recovers the flag without running the binary.

sections.heading: Day 19
sections.title: Flag Printer 20XX: corrupting CPython's small integers
sections.summary: One byte written through /proc/self/mem changes what the cached integer 6 means, which redirects a string index to the hidden part of the flag.

sections.heading: Day 20
sections.title: xorshift521: skipping 521^271441 iterations with linear algebra
sections.summary: The generator is a linear map over GF(2), so the impossible loop becomes one matrix power with a reduced exponent.

sections.heading: Day 27
sections.title: Style Your Alpaca: leaking a flag with CSS alone
sections.summary: JavaScript is blocked, but img-src * and attribute selectors leak the flag one letter at a time through background-image requests.

sections.heading: Day 28
sections.title: Only forward: canary leak plus ret2win
sections.summary: A format-string bug leaks the stack canary and an overflow returns into win() on a non-PIE binary.

sections.heading: Day 19
sections.title: no-win-func: ret2libc from a printf leak
sections.summary: No win() and NX enabled, so a leaked printf address and a two-gadget ROP chain call system("/bin/sh"). All Linux work done in Docker from Windows.

sections.heading: Day 25
sections.title: what-is-my-pointer: safe-linking leaks the heap
sections.summary: A use-after-free read on a tcache chunk exposes safe-linking's shifted pointer, which is enough to point an arbitrary read at the flag.

sections.heading: Day 18-20
sections.title: wrong-instruction: undoing four anti-disassembly tricks in IDA
sections.summary: A misaligned jump, a return-address trampoline, disguised code and an opaque predicate hide a one-line per-byte check.

sections.heading: Day 21-23
sections.title: greetings-i18n-2: from str.format injection to bytecode
sections.summary: A format-string injection walks an exception's traceback into module globals, leaks the checker's code object, and the check is inverted offline.

sections.heading: Day 19-21
sections.title: nested eval: the jail hands you its own blacklist
sections.summary: The banned characters live in a global list, and an f-string rebuilds them by index.

sections.heading: Day 22-24
sections.title: The 3rd: ECDLP over a modulus with a secret prime
sections.summary: The secret third prime never matters. Two small public primes, CRT and a known flag format pin the scalar down exactly.

sections.heading: Day 27-30
sections.title: what is my pointer 2: walking __environ to the flag
sections.summary: With a printf leak and an 8-byte arbitrary read, __environ leads to the stack, where the flag lives only as an environment variable.

notes.title: fsbase-modification: making the stack canary zero
notes.summary: Pointing the FS base at zero-filled BSS turns the stack canary into a known value, and the overflow becomes a plain ret2win.

notes.title: Position-independent code on x86-64: GOT, PLT and lazy binding
notes.summary: Following one global and one function call from the compiler's placeholder zeros, through the linker's offsets and ld.so's relocations, to the first lazy-binding resolve in GDB.

notes.title: Metacognitive traps when coding with AI
notes.summary: Eight ways I've noticed my own problem-solving go wrong, several of them made worse by AI code completion.

notes.title: IronFeather: reversing a drone's custom KDF to rebuild its crash
notes.summary: A stripped PX4 binary hides a 384-round ARX key derivation. Reimplementing it decrypts the mission store and the flight log, which show the payload release, an injected motor failure and the crash site.
